title: Three ways a choice can matter

data.source: Three standard toy systems from Phoenix study ETERNITY-AND-FINITUDE-2026-10-06 (checks 2a to 2d): a fading average, a ball at a fork between two valleys (600 seeded histories here), and the logistic map.

prediction: A choice can matter in three standard ways: it fades below notice after about 66 later occasions when memory keeps nine tenths each time; it lasts for good when it picks a branch at a fork and later noise is small; and in a chaotic system it grows for good but cannot be traced back.
baseline: The standard results themselves: a geometric series, Kramers' escape time (1940) and the sensitivity of chaotic maps. They give every number here without CRR.
why: The three sums come out as Phoenix records them, and they are ordinary mathematics. What CRR adds is a reading: that the branch choices are what a history is made of, and that this is a reason to care. Phoenix calls that a value, not a theorem, and no observation has been named that could count against it.
